headline: K 2750 floods first - limit 13% not 20%
summary: Column flooding hits 110% of the 0.8 Fair limit at +20% feed (0.876 vs 0.8 in run K2750_1p2) so the plant can only reach 1.13× feed before flooding (process_capacity). Holding reflux needs +33% heat: reboiler 427 to 570 kW and condenser 423 to 565 kW (K2750_base → K2750_1p2); hardware to keep spec is a 600-650 mm ID shell ~ $100k-$1M, operating at lower reflux is free but cuts separation.

why: Process capacity shows flood is the only limit - at 1.2× Fair flood 0.876 exceeds 0.8 (109.5% util) while T and P are <61% of 6 bar/150C design (K2750_1p2). Cheapest compliant operating move is reflux 1.5→0.8 (run K2750_1p2_R0p8 79% util) with no capex but product purity penalty. To keep current separation at 1.2× the hydraulics need 0.642 m (K2750_1p2), so a 600 mm ID column gives 0.608 flood (76% util, K2750_1p2_d0p60) and 650 mm gives margin; stainless 14 m column retray/replacement is $100k-$1M class, plus ~33% extra heat (143 kW) - conclusion provisional until feed spec, purity spec and KX 2750 geometry are confirmed by field checks.

headline: Flooding limits K 2750 at 1.13x, not 1.2x
summary: K 2750 on P&ID ProcessColumn-1 (500 mm ID, 6 bar/150C) reaches 80% Fair flood at 1.13x feed (process_capacity on K2750_base_run). At 1.2x with design reflux 1.5 flood is 0.876 vs 0.8 = 109.5% (K2750_1p2_run) with +34% heat: reboiler 427 to 570 kW, condenser 423 to 565 kW. Reducing reflux to 0.8 or replacing shell with 600 mm ID (matching KX 2750 enlarged section) passes all P/T and flood checks at 1.2x with no other data-limited checks failing.
